analyzed_vuln.description: The Kerberos dissector stores attacker-controlled cname data into `flow->protos.kerberos.username` before conclusively claiming the flow as Kerberos. In particular, the AS-REQ (`msg_type == 0x0A`) path writes the username but does not call `ndpi_int_kerberos_add_connection`. Because `flow->protos` is a union, `kerberos.username` overlaps the TLS/QUIC pointer fields; its first bytes overlap `flow->protos.stun_ssl.ssl.tls_supported_versions`. A later dissector can therefore classify the same flow as TLS/QUIC, after which `ndpi_free_flow` interprets the attacker-controlled username bytes as an allocated pointer and passes them to `ndpi_free`, causing the wild-address read in ASan's allocator.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A UDP packet using Kerberos port 88 must be long enough to enter the detailed parser (`payload_packet_len > 128`) and satisfy its heuristic AS-REQ structure checks so attacker-controlled cname bytes are copied into `flow->protos.kerberos.username`. The AS-REQ path leaves the protocol uncommitted, allowing the same packet to subsequently be recognized as TLS or QUIC. When the harness calls `ndpi_free_flow`, the TLS/QUIC cleanup branch is selected and frees the overlapping non-pointer value (the PoV fills it with `0xff` bytes), producing the invalid free. Patch the Kerberos path so it does not populate union-owned Kerberos fields unless it also commits/exclusively owns the flow, or explicitly mark valid AS-REQ packets as Kerberos before other dissectors can reinterpret the union.

I am considering either parsing into locals and committing before copying, or simply classifying the AS-REQ as Kerberos once the existing structural msg_type checks pass, before/after metadata writes. Please assess intended behavior and any false-positive or control-flow concerns.
